problemStatement.formal:
Let $\mathrm{ex}_r(n;K_{r+1}^r)$ be the maximum number of $r$-edges that can be placed on $n$ vertices without forming a $K_{r+1}^r$ (the $r$-uniform complete graph on $r+1$ vertices).

Is every $r$-hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices the union of at most $\mathrm{ex}_{r}(n;K_{r+1}^r)$ many copies of $K_r^r$ and $K_{r+1}^r$, no two of which share a $K_r^r$?



A conjecture of Erd\H{o}s and Sauer.

# Erdős #719 - Knowledge Base

## Problem Statement

Let ex_r(n; K_{r+1}^r) be the Turán number for r-uniform hypergraphs.

Conjecture (Erdős–Sauer, 1981): Every r-uniform hypergraph G on n vertices is the union of at most ex_r(n; K_{r+1}^r) copies of K_r^r and K_{r+1}^r, with no two sharing a K_r^r.

## Status

**Erdős Database Status**: OPEN
**Tractability Score**: 5/10
**Aristotle Suitable**: Partially (structural lemmas only)
